_comment: REPO-ROOT-tier build description for libxml2 v2.15.3 (commit c94eb0210183b9d7cb43f8e7fddc6be55843ef49).
Authoritative for library partitioning, link topology and build
libxml2 is the simplest topology of the four evaluation targets: ONE
shared object, 55 .c files flat at the repo root, public headers under
include/libxml/, private headers under include/private/. There is no
vendored third-party source - every dependency is a system library - so
the in-tree / out-of-tree split needs no judgement call here.
_comment_executables: Built by the same cmake run and present in the CodeQL database, but
outside the target: oracle-config.json names only include/libxml/, so
none of their entities enters scope. Recorded for link-topology
_comment_features: DOCUMENTATION ONLY - no composer reads this. The authoritative record
of what compiled is the CodeQL database, which is anchored on the
configure line below. Listed because a reader deciding whether a gap is
real needs to know which subsystems this build even contains.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_OUTPUT
all.role: Serialization support - xmlsave.h and xmlwriter.h. Default ON. Load-bearing for this campaign: xmlwriter is 81 of the 1416 public functions and the largest single block the hand-written crate leaves at 0% coverage.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_VALID
all.role: DTD validation - valid.h, 71 functions, also 0% covered by the hand-written crate. Default ON.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_SAX1
all.role: The older SAX1 interface. Default ON. SAX2.h (36 fns) is unconditional; SAX.h is the SAX1 shim.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_CATALOG
all.role: Catalog resolution - catalog.h, 37 functions, 0% covered. Default ON.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_XPATH
all.role: XPath - xpath.h (41) + xpathInternals.h (117). The internals header is the second-largest gap. Default ON.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_THREADS
all.role: Multithread support. Default ON. Note libxml2's global memory management is documented as not thread-safe; a generated wrapper inherits that, it does not fix it.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_ICONV
all.role: Character-set conversion via iconv. Default ON; glibc provides iconv, so no extra link entry.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_ZLIB
all.role: Compressed input/output. Adds the libz link edge.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_MODULES
all.role: Dynamic module loading - xmlmodule.h. Adds the libdl link edge. Default ON.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_HTTP
all.role: ABI compatibility shim for the REMOVED HTTP support. Default OFF upstream and left OFF - nanohttp.h still declares 17 functions but they are stubs.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_LEGACY
all.role: Deprecated APIs kept for compatibility. Default OFF and left OFF: wrapping a deprecated surface is not the campaign's goal.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_ICU
all.role: ICU as the encoding backend, alternative to iconv. Default OFF, left OFF - one encoding backend is enough and ICU pulls in a large C++ dependency.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_TLS
all.role: Thread-local storage for the global state. Default OFF at this tag.

all.name: LIBXML2_WITH_PYTHON
all.role: Python bindings. OFF - not C the campaign wraps.

_comment_test_baseline: NOT YET COLLECTED. Phase 1 step 4 fills this: run `configure`, `build`,
then `test`, and record pass/total plus the name of every test disabled
to reach a green run. A post-wrap run must match it.
For a wrap-only campaign the baseline plays a different role than in a
port: no C body is replaced, so the C test suite cannot regress. It is
recorded anyway as the reference the generated wrapper's own round-trip
tests are judged against, and to prove the build the CodeQL database was
traced from is a working one.
_comment_static_build_commands: The staticlib variant the Rust side links against. Sanitizers off and
programs/tests off: this build exists to be linked, not run.
_comment_codeql_database: NOT YET BUILT. Phase 1 step 5. Sanitizers are OFF here and tests are
ON: the database must contain the test translation units so the
footprint analysis can see how the API is actually called, which is a
large part of what a wrap campaign infers ownership from. `fill in on
creation` markers below are for the orchestrator.
Host arch matters: an x86_64 database against an aarch64 host silently
skews the type layouts the wrapper is generated from. Record both.
